criteria.criterion: `rebar bridge`, `rebar bridge --help`, `rebar bridge preview --help`, and `rebar bridge sync --help` expose only functional `preview` and `sync` verbs with pinned exit/stream contracts.
An unknown nested verb fails with valid choices and never dispatches a same-named top-level command.
`bridge preview` performs zero Jira writes and zero ticket or bridge-state writes, proven by exact snapshots and the fake transport log.
`bridge sync` performs a persisted mutation from a production-shaped fake Jira fixture while preserving unrelated state.
`--mode`, `--filter-local-ids`, and unknown arguments are rejected on both verbs.
Captured `bridge`, `preview`, and `sync` help contains none of `mode`, `rank`, `gate`, `lock`, `cap`, `pass`, `binding store`, or numeric exit-code values.

`Mode`, `MODE_CAPS`, and `gated_mode: "reconcile-check"` remain intact and exercised by `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/orchestrate/test_mode.py` and `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_advisory_lock.py`.

Top-level `doctor`, `reconcile`, `jira-onboard`, `bridge-probe`, and `bridge-fsck` behavior remains unchanged; continuity is exercised by `tests/interfaces/facades/test_bridge_cli_heldout.py::test_legacy_reconcile_keeps_dry_run_default` plus the existing suites.

`scripts/gen_cli_reference.py` generates the nested group, proven by `tests/unit/test_gen_cli_reference.py::test_render_expands_the_staged_bridge_group`; `docs/cli-reference.md`, `docs/exit-codes.md`, `docs/user-guide.md`, and `docs/release-notes.md` describe only the staged surface that ships.
